user.description: Add a UniFi OS console with a gateway (for example a Dream Machine or a Cloud Gateway). Use a local user of the console; the read-only role is enough.

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the console, for example 192.168.1.1.
data_description.username: A local user of the console, not a UI.com account.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off only if the console uses its own self-signed certificate.
data_description.use_admin: For the switch "Enforce backup uplink", which switches the preferred uplink off in the console, and the buttons "Run speed test" and "Run speed test over backup uplink". Asks for separate admin credentials in the next step; without them the integration never writes.

reconfigure.description: Change the address, the user or the certificate check.

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the console, for example 192.168.1.1.
data_description.username: A local user of the console, not a UI.com account.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off only if the console uses its own self-signed certificate.
data_description.use_admin: For the switch "Enforce backup uplink", which switches the preferred uplink off in the console, and the buttons "Run speed test" and "Run speed test over backup uplink". Asks for separate admin credentials in the next step; without them the integration never writes.

reauth_confirm.description: The console at {host} rejected the login of {username}. Enter the current password.

data_description.password: The password of the local user.

admin.title: Admin credentials
admin.description: A second local user of the console with the admin role for the Network application. It is used only to switch the preferred uplink and to start speed tests, and is stored apart from the read-only credentials.

data_description.admin_username: A local user with the admin role for Network, not a UI.com account.

error.cannot_connect: The console does not answer. Check the address and, if the console has a self-signed certificate, the certificate check.
error.invalid_auth: The console rejected the username or the password.
error.no_gateway: The console has no gateway in its UniFi Network application.
error.admin_invalid_auth: The console rejected the admin credentials.
error.not_admin: This user may not change the Network configuration. It needs the admin role for the Network application.

abort.already_configured: This gateway is already set up.
abort.wrong_gateway: This console has a different gateway than the one set up.

run_backup_speedtest.name: Run speed test over backup uplink

gateway_missing.message: The console no longer reports the gateway.

no_admin.message: This needs admin credentials; add them with Reconfigure.

no_wan_config.message: The preferred uplink is not found in the console's configuration.

backup_already_active.message: The backup uplink already carries the traffic; the preferred uplink is not switched off.

lte_data_plan_used.message: The LTE data plan is {percent} % used (limit {limit} %); the preferred uplink is not switched off.

speedtest_running.message: A speed test is already running; wait until it is finished.

backup_speedtest_running.message: A speed test over the backup uplink is already in progress.

admin_login_rejected.message: The console rejected the admin credentials; check them with Reconfigure.

admin_not_allowed.message: The admin user may not change the Network configuration.

console_write_failed.message: The console did not take the change: {error}

speedtest_not_started.message: The console did not start the speed test: {error}

data.auto_off_minutes: Enforce backup uplink: switch back after
data.lte_limit_percent: Enforce backup uplink: refuse from an LTE usage of

data_description.auto_off_minutes: Minutes after which the preferred uplink is switched on again by itself. In a test, about 60 MB per minute ran over LTE.
data_description.lte_limit_percent: Percent of the LTE data plan from which the switch refuses to switch on.
data_description.expected_speed_wan: What the WAN port should negotiate, in Mbit/s, for example 2500 for a 2.5G port. Empty or 0: not checked. With a value, a binary sensor turns on while the port negotiated less or half duplex.
data_description.expected_speed_wan2: What the WAN port should negotiate, in Mbit/s, for example 2500 for a 2.5G port. Empty or 0: not checked. With a value, a binary sensor turns on while the port negotiated less or half duplex.
data_description.expected_speed_wan3: What the WAN port should negotiate, in Mbit/s, for example 2500 for a 2.5G port. Empty or 0: not checked. With a value, a binary sensor turns on while the port negotiated less or half duplex.
data_description.expected_speed_wan4: What the WAN port should negotiate, in Mbit/s, for example 2500 for a 2.5G port. Empty or 0: not checked. With a value, a binary sensor turns on while the port negotiated less or half duplex.

console_unreachable.title: {title}: console not reachable
console_unreachable.description: The console has not answered for {minutes} minutes; the entities are unavailable until it does. Check the console, its address and the way to it. The address can be changed with Reconfigure. This issue goes away with the next successful poll.

lte_limit_disabled.title: {title}: LTE data limit turned off
lte_limit_disabled.description: The data limit of {name} is turned off in UniFi Network. The sensor "LTE data used" stays unknown, and the switch "Enforce backup uplink" cannot refuse near the limit. Turn the limit on in UniFi Network under the LTE device's settings, or ignore this issue if you do not want one.

admin_not_allowed.title: {title}: admin user cannot write
admin_not_allowed.description: The admin user of the admin features does not work: {reason}. The switch "Enforce backup uplink" and the speed test buttons will fail. Give the user the admin role for the Network application in UniFi OS, or change the credentials with Reconfigure. This issue goes away once a check succeeds.
